h1: American-style press brake tooling — punches and dies with the .500″ tang
intro: EUROSTAMP punches and dies with the American tang — .500″ (12.7 mm) wide with the safety lip — for the American-style clamping found on most press brakes built in North America. Punches stand 3.779″ (96 mm) high: 88° straight and 88° / 85° gooseneck punches for 90° air bending, 30° and 28° acute punches for hemming and acute angles, and a 5.125″ acute gooseneck. The dies all share a 1.937″ (49.2 mm) working height: 88° dies V .375 to .750″ and 30° – 34° acute dies V .375 to .875″. Every tool comes in 36″ and 18″ lengths and a 35.75″ sectioned set, each with its own part number. For press brakes with European-style (Amada-Promecam) clamping there is a Z1 intermediate that takes these punches.

faq.q: Will American-style tooling fit my press brake?
faq.a: It fits press brakes with American-style clamping — a .500″ tang in a clamp bar, used on most press brakes built in North America. Measure the tang slot of your upper clamp and lower die holder, or send us a photo of a tool you use now, and we confirm. If your brake has European-style clamping, see the European punches and dies pages — or, to use American-style punches on it, the Z1 intermediate on this page, for brakes built for Z1 intermediates.

faq.q: Why do the drawings say the dimensions are in inches?
faq.a: American-style tooling is designed in inches. The tables give each dimension in decimal inches with the exact metric value, and the part numbers carry the length in millimetres: 0914 for 36″, 0457 for 18″ and 0908 for the 35.75″ sectioned set.
